description.en: LongDS-Bench evaluates long-horizon, multi-turn data analysis tasks where agents must maintain, update, restore, and compose evolving analytical states. It comprises 68 tasks from real-world Kaggle notebooks spanning 2,225 turns across six domains, with an average dependency span of 11.3 turns.

evidence.snippet: We introduce LongDS, a benchmark for long-horizon, multi-turn data analysis where agents must maintain, update, restore, and compose evolving analytical states.

claire_radar.motivation: Real-world data analysis is inherently iterative, yet existing benchmarks mostly evaluate isolated or short interactive tasks, leaving agents' ability to track evolving analytical context over long horizons untested.

claire_radar.paperTitle: LongDS-Bench: On the Failure of Long-Horizon Agentic Data Analysis

source.title: LongDS-Bench: On the Failure of Long-Horizon Agentic Data Analysis

claire_radar.whyItMatters: Existing benchmarks focus on isolated or short interactive tasks, leaving long-horizon analytical state management untested. This benchmark reveals a critical bottleneck in agent performance, where errors concentrate in later turns and additional interaction steps do not reliably improve accuracy, aiding development of more reliable agentic systems.
